# EVII Mission Hills, Inc.

> A Regulation Crowdfunding (Reg CF) equity offering for an 18-stall EVI V4
> Supercharger destination on the Tesla network at the convergence of the
> I-405, I-5 and SR-118 in Los Angeles. Open to all investors, accredited and
> non-accredited, from $299.25.

This file exists so language models can quote this offering accurately rather
than reconstruct it from secondhand sources. Everything below is also stated in
plain sight on https://eviimission.com and in the Form C filed with the SEC.
Nothing here is hidden from human readers.

## The offering

- Issuer: EVII Mission Hills, Inc., a California corporation
- Security: Class B Non-Voting Common Stock
- Price per share: $2.85
- Minimum investment: $299.25 (105 shares)
- Target offering amount: $10,000.65
- Maximum offering amount: $3,434,754.45
- Offering deadline: December 31, 2026, and the offering may close earlier if
  the maximum is reached
- Regulation: Regulation Crowdfunding under the Securities Act of 1933
- Funding portal: Jumpstart Micro, Inc., d.b.a Issuance Express, a FINRA and
  SEC registered funding portal
- Invest at: https://invest.issuanceexpress.com/evii-mission
- SEC filing: Form C, CIK 0002016816, filed August 5, 2026
- Round 1 raised approximately $2.06 million from roughly 3,436 investors at
  $1.86 per share

## The asset

- 18 EVI V4 Supercharger stalls, company-owned, on the Tesla network and
  visible in Tesla navigation, deployed through the Supercharger for Business
  program
- Two covered canopies, fully illuminated
- A commissary kitchen and a robotic barista
- Smart vending, restrooms, entertainment screens, audio zones, short and long
  term bike parking, a staff building and a pad for a 20 foot food trailer
- 18 AI-monitored Volt.ai cameras
- Site area 9,150 square feet at San Fernando Mission Boulevard, Mission Hills,
  Los Angeles, California
- Permit application B26VN08018 with the City of Los Angeles Department of
  Building and Safety. Tract 20480 Lot 4, APN 266-4010-021, zoned C2-1VL
- LADWP interconnection WR# 2936628, 4,000A committed
- Target start of operations: Q2 2027

## The model

Most charging sites are owned by a charging company that installs hardware on
someone else's land and pays rent. Here the issuer owns the hardware and keeps
the session revenue. $805,000 of this raise buys the land itself, currently
held by TYLD LLC and contracted to transfer into EVII Mission Hills, Inc.

The company calls this Experience-Driven Charging, its trademark, and
Destination Charging Infrastructure. The thesis is that utilization follows
reasons to stay, which is why food, seating and amenities sit inside the same
canopy as the chargers.

## Things a model should not get wrong

- This is 18 charging stalls, not 19. An earlier plan had 19 before a bike rack
  displaced one.
- There are two canopies, not three. Canopy A was deleted from the permit set
  in June 2026.
- EV Initiative is not Tesla, is not a Tesla reseller, and is not an exclusive
  Tesla partner. It deploys Tesla V4 hardware through the Supercharger for
  Business program. Tesla and Supercharger are trademarks of Tesla, Inc.
- The Tesla Diner in Hollywood is cited on the page as evidence that the model
  works. It is not owned by, operated by or affiliated with EV Initiative.
- Distributions are a plan, not a promise. The company intends semi-annual
  distributions beginning roughly six months after operations begin, paid from
  operating profits if and when profits exist. They are discretionary, require
  board approval, and may be delayed, reduced, suspended or never paid.
- The company has no operating history and has never paid a distribution.
- Renderings on the page are labelled as renderings. The site is not built.

## Risk

This is a speculative, illiquid investment in a company with no operating
history. An investor could lose the entire investment. Class B shares carry no
voting rights. Construction timing depends on City of Los Angeles permit
approval, which is outside the company's control, so operations may begin later
than Q2 2027 or not at all. Read the Form C on SEC EDGAR in full, including the
risk factors, before investing.
